newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says U.S. copper costs at US80 cts/lb.
newsitem.headline: BHP says U.S. copper costs at US80 cts/lb.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday its North American copper costs were running at an average of 80 U.S. cents a pound.
"The average is just on 80 cents," said Jim Lewis, head of BHP's copper division.
"It's roughly line ball with the previous quarter -- that's quarter two -- and in terms of where it is relative to where Magma was performing pre-acquisition, it's a deterioration ..."
Lewis said the Arizonal-based Magma operations, acquired in 1995, was operating at about six or seven U.S. cents a pound higher than the average 74 cents a pound before the acquisition.
Lewis balmed the rising costs on problems at the Kalamazoo, Arizona mine, where the BHP has hit delays in developing a high-grade section of the deposit, know as Lower K.
